//: World-building catalogue for the Library (not rules data): regions, factions and groups of the Warhammer world, each summarised in our own words from mordheimer.net lore pages (read 21.10.2026 and 22.10.2026) and, for places and groups mordheimer.net leaves out, from the Warhammer Fantasy Wiki on Fandom (read through its API, 22.10.2026 and 26.10.2026) – never copied. Only entries with more than a subordinate clause of lore are listed. Every entry names its source; nothing here is playable. Kinds: region, faction, group. Places nest (parent), factions and groups come from places (regions); ADR 0024. Tags (TAGS, wish #176, 31.10.2026) are the project's own: a closed list of what belongs together (chaos, undead, elves ...), set by hand on each entry, so a search finds the Norse under Chaos; a tag lists those who serve a thing and, where the list says so, those who fight it.

LORE.name: Mordheim
LORE.status: The ruined City of the Damned, in Ostermark
LORE.text: The capital of Ostermark, crowded with revellers from all over the Empire when the twin-tailed comet fell on the first day of 2000 and destroyed it. Fires and a glowing green miasma hung over the ruins for days. Then the first wyrdstone was found there, which drew treasure hunters, the Empire's rulers and every kind of monster. Inside, the air itself is poisonous and no law holds: it is kill or be killed.

LORE.name: The Pit
LORE.status: The crater where the hammer of Sigmar fell
LORE.text: Where the comet struck, a pit remains whose edges are still hot and whose sides are glassy, as if the rock had run molten. The dead of the city can be seen in the glass, still posed as on that last night. Foul smoke rises from fissures in it. It is said that the Shadowlord, Master of the Possessed, dwells deep in the crater, and daemonic creatures come out of it to infest the ruins.

LORE.name: Temple of Sigmar's Rock
LORE.status: The Sisters' convent on an island in the River Stir
LORE.text: The convent of the Sisters of Sigmar stands on a tall rocky island in the River Stir, which divides Mordheim in two. It survived the destruction unharmed. The Sisters say their unending prayer saved them; the Witch Hunters claim a daemonic pact let them betray the city and escape. The height of the rock lifts them above the poisonous vapours.

LORE.name: Sigmarhaven
LORE.status: A tent camp outside the walls with paid watchmen
LORE.text: One of the shabby fortified settlements that grew up outside the ruins. For all its disorder it is safe enough: paid watchmen keep the peace, and it holds a market for arms sellers, sutlers and victuallers whose wares fetch inflated prices.

LORE.name: Cutthroat's Den
LORE.status: A nest of murderers outside the walls
LORE.text: An encampment little better than a den of murderers. Mutants walk freely there, and hooded men barter corpses to Necromancers in return for tainted gold.

LORE.name: Ostermark
LORE.status: Eastern province of the Empire, lawless since Mordheim fell
LORE.text: One of the largest provinces, on the eastern fringe of the Empire: flat farmland, pasture and hedges, with isolated farms and villages and crude dirt roads, and the Great Forest on the border to Talabecland. Its Elector, Count Steinhardt, died with his whole line when Mordheim fell, and since then brigands, mercenary bands and foreign armies roam it. Famine follows burnt fields, and Orcs and Goblins from the Worlds Edge Mountains and Beastmen from the Forest of Shadows threaten it. Wyrdstone fragments lie scattered across the whole province. Its towns are Bechafen and Badenhof, and its colours are yellow and purple.

LORE.name: The Eerie Downs
LORE.status: A haunted fog-bound plain south of Bechafen
LORE.text: A wide open plain with an unnerving stillness. A permanent low fog rolls over the grass and crags jut from it like broken teeth. Travellers lost there are driven mad by the silence and the loss of direction. It is said the souls of the dead who died there still haunt it and howl at midnight, hungry for more souls.

LORE.name: The Ostermark Marches
LORE.status: Frontier with Kislev, guarded by beacon towers
LORE.text: The border lands to Kislev in the north, marked by wooden watch towers with warning beacons that are lit when invasion looms, and backed by the river Lower Talabec. The town of Bechafen lies deep in the Marches: a military town renowned for the smithies and armourers who supply the army of Ostermark, and so a valuable resource against Chaos from the north.

LORE.name: Reikland
LORE.status: Heart of the Empire; seat of the Temple of Sigmar
LORE.text: Its greatest city is Altdorf, home of the Grand Theogonist. Siegfried, who styles himself Grand Prince, claims the throne with the Grand Theogonist's backing and is opposed most strongly by Middenheim and the Priests of Ulric. Reiklanders are devout followers of Sigmar, known for discipline, loyalty between officers and men and good archery. They wear practical wargear and coloured ribbons for identification or rank, and sneer at the Count of Middenheim as the “lap-dog of Ulric”. Count Siegfried's alchemist van Hoffman is said to have turned lead into gold with wyrdstone.

LORE.name: Middenheim
LORE.status: City of the White Wolf, in Middenland
LORE.text: A city on a mountain pinnacle among dark forest, sacred to Ulric, god of wolves and winter, whose priesthood is still strong there. Its Count, Mannfred Todbringer, is a chief contender for the throne, and the old rivalry with Reikland (and friction with the Temple of Sigmar) goes back hundreds of years. Middenheimers are big, strong, ferocious men, often bare-headed with long hair and beards, who wear wolf pelts as the mark of a wolf killed by hand.

LORE.name: Marienburg
LORE.status: The City of Gold, largest port of the Old World
LORE.text: The most prosperous trading city of the Old World, where goods arrive from Ulthuan to Cathay and every craft is turned to profit. Merchant guilds hold great power there, above all the Freetraders, and its Burgomeisters wield patronage greater than many nobles. Its champion for the throne is Lady Magritta; the Grand Theogonist's refusal to crown her drove a wedge between the city and the Temple of Sigmar. Its warbands are lavishly dressed but ruthless, skilled in duelling and poison, and their rank and file are dockland thugs and ship's crews in leather coats and bandanas. Others mock Marienburgers as popinjays, but many envy their security.

LORE.name: Talabecland
LORE.status: Ostermark's main neighbour, home of the Ottilans
LORE.text: The neighbouring province across the Great Forest, with the city of Talabheim. When the last Emperor, Sigismund, was killed at Altdorf and the Empire split into three claimants, Ostermark sided with the Ottilans of Talabecland. The alliance came to nothing when Magritta of Marienburg took power, and civil war and rivalry followed.

LORE.name: The Grand Prince of Reikland
LORE.status: Claimant to the throne, backed by the Grand Theogonist
LORE.text: Siegfried, ruler of Reikland, who calls himself Grand Prince. He is among the richest and most ambitious contenders and hires mercenaries to bring him wyrdstone. His claim is supported by the Grand Theogonist and opposed by the Count of Middenheim and the Priests of Ulric.

LORE.name: The Count of Middenheim
LORE.status: Mannfred Todbringer, claimant and rival of Reikland
LORE.text: Mannfred Todbringer, one of the chief contenders for the throne and a sponsor of mercenary warbands in Mordheim. He is backed by the Priesthood of Ulric and in constant friction with the Temple of Sigmar.

LORE.name: Lady Magritta of Marienburg
LORE.status: The merchant guilds' candidate for the throne
LORE.text: The favourite of the merchant guilds and the common choice of the lesser states. The Grand Theogonist disqualified her under the doctrine of male ascent, by which no woman may wear Sigmar's crown. The Ostermark account has her as the young Empress who secured power, though many in the powerful institutions around Altdorf thought her a puppet of her elders.

LORE.name: The Freetraders
LORE.status: Secret circle of the richest guildsmen
LORE.text: The High Order of Honourable Freetraders, an elite and secretive body of wealthy merchants based in Marienburg. They feel shackled by the old order and want power, and their candidate for Emperor is Lady Magritta. Their secret members hold positions of authority throughout the Empire, and through them most minor Electors were persuaded to back her. The Grand Theogonist has set himself against them. Some of those disappointed by the old order are said to turn to dark cults and sorcery.

LORE.name: Count von Carstein of Sylvania
LORE.status: Powerful claimant, secretly a necromancer and vampire
LORE.text: The most powerful of the other claimants, though few are tempted by his gold because of his reputation: he is said to drink the blood of men and raise the dead. His minions are sly, skulk in the shadows and avoid daylight, yet they too come to Mordheim. Few suspect his true nature, perhaps only the Witch Hunters, who trust no one.

LORE.name: The Grand Theogonist of Sigmar
LORE.status: Spiritual head of the Empire, hungry for worldly power
LORE.text: The leader of the Temple of Sigmar, whose temples stand in every town. He refused to crown Lady Magritta and is said to covet the crown himself. He preaches a holy crusade against mutants and sorcerers, and has sent the Witch Hunters into Mordheim, officially to cleanse it, but, it is said, also to gather wyrdstone for his own ends. Since the city fell, thousands have gathered at the holy places and penitents roam the roads.

LORE.name: The Witch Hunters
LORE.status: Templars of Sigmar who persecute heretics
LORE.text: The Order of Templars, called Witch Hunters by those who fear and hate them and by themselves, who take pride in persecuting heretics. They came to Mordheim with carts of cages, braziers and irons. They trust no one, curse the Sisters of Sigmar as heretics for their creed that denies women divinity in Sigmar's temple, and are ancient enemies of the Sisterhood.

LORE.name: The Sisters of Sigmar
LORE.status: Holy Order, home of the Seeress who read the comet
LORE.text: The Holy Order whose Seeress first saw the comet. Its members are daughters of the noblest houses of the Empire, and its cloisters have long sheltered those who would be troublesome to their families. Their convent, the Temple of Sigmar's Rock, survived the destruction. They fight side by side with the Witch Hunters yet are their deadliest enemies, in a holy rivalry that no forgiveness can end.

LORE.name: The Shadowlord and the Cult of the Possessed
LORE.de: Der Schattenherr und der Kult der Besessenen
LORE.status: Dark Emperor of the secret cults, said to dwell in the Pit
LORE.text: The secret cults of the dark gods, made up of those who found the old order a shackle, and who practise sorcery, have found a leader: the Shadowlord, Master of the Possessed, a Dark Emperor of whom none can say whether he is man or Daemon. The cults gather wyrdstone in Mordheim. From the crater come twisted daemonic creatures of great strength that infest the ruins.

LORE.name: The Ostermark Warbands
LORE.status: Farmers turned fighters, defending what is left
LORE.text: Farmers by trade, sturdy and capable fighters who have defended their land alone against mercenaries and brigands. Since Mordheim fell, some have abandoned burnt farms and formed warbands to take back what was taken, to defend their land, or simply to share the plunder. Their men do not give up easily and their captains may start with a wardog from the farm. They fight with pitchforks, axes and bows, and carry wooden shields and the heraldry of rams, bulls' heads, scythes and ears of corn.

LORE.name: The Brigands and Reavers of Ostermark
LORE.de: Die Räuber und Plünderer von Ostermark
LORE.status: Bandits and roaming mercenary bands in the ruined countryside
LORE.text: Since the fall of Mordheim, wild reavers, thieves, bandits and mercenary bands roam the neglected province, loot villages, burn homes and rob the weak. The only law they know is force of arms. Some fighters rise up against them out of a sense of justice, which the lawless time rarely rewards.

LORE.name: Old World
LORE.status: Home continent of the human realms and of Mordheim
LORE.text: The western lands where the Empire, Kislev, Bretonnia and Tilea lie, cut off from the dwarfen and orc lands by great mountain ranges. Merchants from here sail to Lustria and the Southlands or trek over land to Ind and Cathay. Most warbands in the campaign start their journey from somewhere in this region.

LORE.name: The Empire
LORE.status: Greatest human realm; no Emperor, split between rival Electors
LORE.text: A huge, heavily forested land ringed by the Sea of Claws, the Worlds Edge, Black and Grey Mountains. Around the year 2000 no Emperor rules and the Elector Counts and the Grand Theogonist fight over the crown, while bandits, mutants and Beastmen roam the wilds. The big electoral provinces, including the Halfling Mootland, each send fortune seekers to Mordheim.

LORE.name: Averland
LORE.status: Rich southern province of the Empire; capital Averheim
LORE.text: A prosperous county between the Aver and the Upper Reik, bordering the Black Mountains and the Worlds Edge Mountains. Its mines supply ore that is barged down the Aver to Nuln, and its soldiers are famed for lavish uniforms and good archery. Mercenaries from here know the Black Fire Pass trade route and its Night Goblin and Skaven dangers.

LORE.name: Hochland
LORE.status: Forested province next to Talabecland, hit hard by the Storm of Chaos
LORE.text: A province across the River Talabec from Talabecland. After the Storm of Chaos many Hochlanders fled across the border as refugees and clashed with the locals around Talabheim. Poverty and scarce trade drive some of them into banditry and into the Great Forest in search of rumoured treasure.

LORE.name: Middenland
LORE.status: Duchy of the Count of Middenheim, land of the Ulric cult
LORE.text: A northern electoral duchy, ruled from the mountaintop city of Middenheim by Count Mannfred Todbringer, one of the leading claimants to the throne. The Drakwald Forest surrounds the city, and the Great North Road leads from here to Marienburg. Its people are big, fierce and loyal to Ulric.

LORE.name: Ostland
LORE.status: Sparse northern province with close ties to Kislev
LORE.text: The thinly populated northernmost province, cut off from the rest of the Empire by the Forest of Shadows and the Middle Mountains. Its poor, hardy villagers live as farmers and trappers, honour Taal, and have suffered more than anyone from Chaos raids. They are self-reliant and will hire no mercenaries save Ogres.

LORE.name: Stirland
LORE.status: County along the River Stir, famed for strict law and outlaws
LORE.text: A county whose Elector Count was feared for harsh justice; even petty criminals were declared outlaws. Many fled north into Stirwood, a small forest across the River Stir near Nuln, where they formed archer bands. Tales of Mordheim travelling down the river tempt such outlaws towards the ruined city.

LORE.name: Sylvania
LORE.status: Province ruled by the von Carsteins, a land of vampires and fog
LORE.text: Count Vlad von Carstein and his Countess rule from Drakenhof castle; the whole ruling class are vampires hiding behind a dire reputation. The land is full of bogs, fogs and the restless dead, so locals either flee or take up arms. Vampire hunters and Morr priests enter to break the dynasty, and Vlad's servants hunt wyrdstone in Mordheim.

LORE.name: Moot
LORE.status: Halfling Mootland, an electoral province of its own
LORE.text: The Halfling homeland where the Aver Reach and the Blue Reach rivers meet. It counts among the Empire's electoral provinces. Halflings seldom leave, but now and then a restless elder gathers friends and marches to Mordheim hoping for gold, wyrdstone and kitchens.

LORE.name: Wasteland
LORE.status: Low, windy, marshy plain around Marienburg
LORE.text: A barren, marshy coastal plain exposed to the winds off the Sea of Claws, running from the Reikwald Forest to the Pale Sisters. Marienburg, the greatest port of the Old World, stands here at the mouth of the Reik. Rumours say Orcs and Beastmen lurk in the fens.

LORE.name: Altdorf
LORE.status: Great Reikland city on an island in the Reik, home of the Grand Theogonist
LORE.text: Reikland's greatest city, built on a mud-flat island where the Talabec meets the Reik, among marshes and shifting channels. It is home to the Grand Theogonist and the Temple of Sigmar and hosts the College of Magic.

LORE.name: Nuln
LORE.status: River city with the Imperial Gunnery School
LORE.text: A great city on the Reik, where the Aver and the Upper Reik join. Its last bridge is a wonder with a liftable wooden centre. It is respected for the best handguns and war machines outside the dwarf holds and trains the Empire's gunners.

LORE.name: Talabheim
LORE.status: Crater city of Talabecland, Taal's stronghold
LORE.text: A large city on the Talabec, which is too wide to bridge here and so needs a big ferry. It is built in a great crater and honours Taal as Father of Rivers. It has strained to absorb refugees from the east, and Horned Hunters stay away from it.

LORE.name: Great Forest
LORE.status: Enormous forest in the heart of the Empire; border of Ostermark and Talabecland
LORE.text: An ancient, huge woodland of old oaks and willows from the Middle Mountains to Nuln, and from Altdorf to Kislev's border. The River Stir cuts off its southern part as Stirwood. Many corners are too wild even for Imperial armies, so small warbands search them for secrets such as the Nemesis Crown.

LORE.name: Forest of Shadows
LORE.status: Dark pine forest covering most of Ostland
LORE.text: A dense, gloomy pine forest north of the Middle Mountains. Bandits, Chaos warbands, Forest Goblins and wolf packs haunt it. The road from Middenheim to Kislev's Erengrad runs through it.

LORE.name: Drakwald Forest
LORE.status: Sparse birch forest around Middenheim
LORE.text: A thin birch forest on poor sandy soil that was never cleared for farming. It lies around Middenheim, and the road from Marienburg to Middenheim crosses it. Several wilderness scenarios are set in its 'Deeps' territory.

LORE.name: Middle Mountains
LORE.status: Highest uplands of the Empire, inhabited by Ogres and Chaos bands
LORE.text: A tall range in the north of the Empire, ringed by dense forest and lacking any dwarf holds. Chaos warbands, Beastmen, Orcs and Goblins use the heights as hideouts, and Ogres live on the peaks. Few humans go there, apart from bandits.

LORE.name: River Reik
LORE.status: Main trade artery of the Empire, from Black Fire Pass to Marienburg
LORE.text: The most important river of the Empire, rising south of Black Fire Pass and flowing to the sea at Marienburg. More ships ply the stretch between Marienburg and Nuln than on all other imperial rivers together. The Reikland on its banks is the most prosperous part of the Empire.

LORE.name: River Stir
LORE.status: River flowing through the ruins of Mordheim
LORE.text: A large river that rises near Karak Kadrin and runs down through the Great Forest in a deep, wooded valley. Stirland lies to its south and Talabecland to its north, and there are few places to cross it. It flows through Mordheim, so rumours of the ruined city travel with it towards Stirland.

LORE.name: Kislev
LORE.status: Northern realm of the Tzars, bulwark against Chaos
LORE.text: A land of forests giving way to steppe toward the Worlds Edge Mountains, with long harsh winters and mostly timber towns, though the old capital has white buildings with gilded domes. It lies right on the edge of the Chaos Wastes and is often raided by Norse. Allied to the Empire, its people are cheerful, fond of vodka and good fighters.

LORE.name: Bretonnia
LORE.status: Realm of chivalry beyond the Grey Mountains
LORE.text: A kingdom of knights ruled by honour and under the Lady of the Lake. Its nobles see Mordheim as a vile place and thus a fitting test, so Questing Knights give up their domain and ride there, trailed by Knights Errant. The main road to the Empire leads over the Grey Mountains.

LORE.name: Athel Loren
LORE.status: Enchanted forest of the Wood Elves, said to lie in eastern Bretonnia
LORE.text: A magical forest where the reclusive Wood Elves have long lived apart from their kin, ruled by Orion and Ariel. They hate Dark Elves and will not fight beside Chaos. Rarely, their warbands step out to shape events beyond the woods.

LORE.name: Tilea
LORE.status: Land of rival merchant city-states and sea traders
LORE.text: A wealthy land of feuding city-states whose people are proud of their civic status and have become skilled sailors and explorers. Tilean warbands are hired by city-states, guilds and merchants to probe jungles, deserts and ruins like Mordheim. Many caravans for the far east have set out from here.

LORE.name: Miragliano
LORE.status: Tilean city of crossbowmen who hate Skaven
LORE.text: A Tilean city famed for its crossbows; its warbands shoot well with them. Its people have hated Skaven since the red pox of 1812 killed three quarters of its inhabitants.

LORE.name: Remas
LORE.status: Tilean port city that loathes Dark Elves
LORE.text: A coastal Tilean city invaded by a Dark Elf fleet in 1487. Its people ever since fight Dark Elves to the death, and its officers are stern leaders. Remas was the one city that refused to back the famous overland caravan to the east.

LORE.name: Trantio
LORE.status: Tilean city whose warbands were best equipped in Lustria
LORE.text: A Tilean city-state that sends well-funded expeditions overseas. In Lustrian campaigns a Trantio warband starts with extra funds and thus counts as the best equipped human band there.

LORE.name: Border Princes
LORE.status: Wild southern lands beyond the Black Mountains
LORE.text: The unruly southern borderland beyond the Black Mountains, outside the Empire's rule. Goods from here come to the Empire through Black Fire Pass.

LORE.name: Black Mountains
LORE.status: Southern mountain wall of the Empire, riddled with goblin tunnels
LORE.text: A steep, hostile range between the Grey and Worlds Edge Mountains that divides the Empire from the Border Princes. The weather is erratic and the passes are dangerous. Night Goblins, Trolls and Skaven infest its crumbly tunnels.

LORE.name: Black Fire Pass
LORE.status: Only reliable pass over the southern mountains
LORE.text: A deep fortified cleft that divides the Black Mountains from the Worlds Edge Mountains and guards the southern approach to the Empire. It follows an old dwarf road past Averheim, and goods go on by barge to Nuln. Sigmar is said to have beaten the Orcs in the valley in its middle.

LORE.name: Grey Mountains
LORE.status: Mountains separating the Empire from Bretonnia
LORE.text: The western range, with few and less rich dwarf holds. Most passes are narrow, fit for merchants with pack animals only, while the biggest, Axe Bite Pass, is guarded by Helmgart. The Gisoreux Gap in the north is the main route between Bretonnia and the Empire.

LORE.name: Worlds Edge Mountains
LORE.status: Huge eastern range of dwarf holds, greenskins and monsters
LORE.text: A very tall range along the eastern side of the Empire and Kislev, with a handful of passes and many underground routes. It holds rich dwarf mines but also Night Goblins, Skaven and monsters, and the ruined holds. Beyond its eastern side lie the Dark Lands, the start of the road to Cathay.

LORE.name: Norsca
LORE.status: Cold northern land of the Norse, across the Sea of Claws
LORE.text: A land of snow, ice and mountains north of the Empire, home to mammoths, big wolves and polar bears. The Norse there live by war and raiding and are superb sailors, and the southern tribes are least touched by Chaos. They were the first humans to find Lustria and the Southlands, and many sell their swords as mercenaries.

LORE.name: The Chaos Wastes
LORE.status: Frozen north where the winds of Chaos blow
LORE.text: A land in the far north from which Chaos spills out, with Kislev lying right at its edge. Kurgan and Hung nomads of the Northern Wastes worship the dark gods, and the Kurgan raise monoliths where the winds of Chaos blow strong. Marauder chieftains lead warbands south to win glory.

LORE.name: Eastern Steppes
LORE.status: Endless grassland north of Cathay roamed by the Hung
LORE.text: A vast plain on the northern edge of Grand Cathay, over which the nomadic Hung range. Hobgoblin riders also roam it, and Cathay built the Great Bastion against such raiders. The mutant Tong horde once swept across it.

LORE.name: Lustria
LORE.status: Jungle continent of the Lizardmen and the lost cities of gold
LORE.text: A steaming continent across the western ocean of ancient ziggurat cities abandoned by the Lizardmen and guarded by their temple guards. Explorers seek gold, magic and arcane lore there and many never return. Norse, Tilean and Estalian colonies hug the coast, with High Elves in the south and a war between Lizardmen and Skaven in the interior.

LORE.name: Skeggi
LORE.status: Oldest human colony in Lustria, founded by the Norse
LORE.text: The Norse port founded by Losteriksson in the year 888 on Lustria's east coast, still home to his descendants. It has faded as the restless Norse sought raids elsewhere, but still offers good mercenaries and drinking halls. The Amazons are said to descend from Norse widows who left here.

LORE.name: Santa Magritta
LORE.status: Estalian jewel of Lustria, on Colombo's Island
LORE.text: A handsome Estalian port with a busy harbour, markets of Old World and exotic goods, and a militia that fights Lizardmen raids and Tileans. Settlers, convicts, mercenaries and missionaries all arrive here. Lizardmen, Amazons, Dark Elves, undead and Skaven warbands may not stay.

LORE.name: Nuevo Luccini
LORE.status: Pirate-and-robber harbour on the Cactus Coast
LORE.text: A lawless Tilean port on the sun-blessed Cactus Coast, known for robbers and pirates but a good place to buy goods. It has taverns, a trading post and a church of Luccan. Rare items cost no extra but all goods are harder to find.

LORE.name: Scorpion Coast
LORE.status: Lustrian coast with the fortified post of the Di Ranza family
LORE.text: A stretch of Lustria's coast where the Tilean Di Ranza family, exiled after feuds, built a fortified trading post. It is used as a staging base for smaller warbands heading into the jungle.

LORE.name: Citadel of Dusk
LORE.status: High Elf fortress on Lustria's southern tip
LORE.text: A huge High Elf stronghold at the southern end of Lustria, where the sun rarely climbs high. It guards the western sea route to Cathay, and the elves send secretive expeditions into the jungle from it. They fight Estalian and Tilean fleets.

LORE.name: Land of the Dead
LORE.status: Desert ruins of Nehekhara, ruled by Tomb Kings and Liches
LORE.text: The old human kingdom of Nehekhara south-east of the Old World, ruined by civil war and now a sand desert with a blood-coloured river. Mummy kings and Liche Lords command legions of the dead in huge necropolises, guarding treasures and necromantic writings. Tomb robbers, Crusaders and Arabian nomads venture in.

LORE.name: Khemri
LORE.status: Cursed city with the Great Pyramid and the Black Pyramid of Nagash
LORE.text: A dead city at the heart of the Land of the Dead, ringed by tombs and crypts of kings and nobles. The Great Pyramid and the vaster Black Pyramid of Nagash dominate it. The dead still patrol and repair the tombs on some dark nights.

LORE.name: Lahmia
LORE.status: Destroyed city of the first vampires, with a burned Great Library
LORE.text: A city of Nehekhara whose destruction ended the kingdom of the Vampires and burned its Great Library. A few Necrarchs fled with Nagash's writings and now hide in towers around the world. Several of them have come to Mordheim.

LORE.name: Araby
LORE.status: Desert land of nomad tribes west of the Land of the Dead
LORE.text: The great desert west of the Land of the Dead where nomad tribes wander from oasis to oasis. They are fine desert guides, feared raiders, and bound by strict honour and blood feuds. Some raid the nearby necropolises.

LORE.name: Cathay and the East
LORE.status: Far eastern lands reached by the long overland roads
LORE.text: The faraway lands of Cathay, Ind and Nippon, long known in the Old World only from rumour. Trade passes by sea around the Southlands or overland through the Dark Lands. Fortunes can be made there, but only a minority of caravans return.

LORE.name: Grand Cathay
LORE.status: Walled eastern empire under the Celestial Emperor
LORE.text: A civilised eastern empire, rich in silk and jade, ruled from Weijin by a divine Emperor and a large bureaucracy. Old Worlders may trade only at a border reservation, and warrior monks guard its fortified frontiers. Monsters, Chaos tribes, Hobgoblins and Ogres press at its borders.

LORE.name: Weijin
LORE.status: Cathayan capital and seat of the Dragon Throne
LORE.text: The city of the Celestial Emperor and his court, entirely devoted to serving the throne. All its food must be brought in from elsewhere, over a hundred tons weekly. The Emperor appoints emissaries from here to govern the border districts.

LORE.name: Great Bastion
LORE.status: Immense wall on Cathay's northern frontier
LORE.text: A seemingly endless wall guarding Cathay's northern border against the Hung. It is at least five men high and runs over hills. Its western end is the city of Nan-Gau, whose garrison patrols its length.

LORE.name: Khuresh
LORE.status: Wild mountain and jungle land south of Cathay
LORE.text: A rough land of mountains, deserts, jungles and marshes on Cathay's southern border. Exiles who want to overthrow the Emperor gather in its north, and ratmen mass there at times. Cathay keeps a second large military command nearby, which also protects the Spice Road to Ind.

LORE.name: Silk Road
LORE.status: Overland caravan route from Tilea to Cathay
LORE.text: The great trade route opened by two Tilean brothers' caravan, passing the last dwarf hold and then crossing the Dark Lands and mountains to reach Cathay. It is deadly: roving greenskins, the restless dead, Chaos dwarfs, Ogres and deserts kill most caravans. Mercenary escorts find steady work here.

LORE.name: Dark Lands
LORE.status: Orc-infested wastes east of the Worlds Edge Mountains
LORE.text: A bleak, desolate plain beyond the dwarf holds, haunted by greenskin wolf riders, wandering undead and dark metal monuments. Chaos dwarfs dominate parts of it from their land of Zharr. Merchants who cross it on the way to Cathay risk everything.

LORE.name: Zharr-Naggrund
LORE.status: City of Fire and Desolation, seat of the Chaos Dwarfs
LORE.text: The Chaos Dwarf city of the Dark Lands, where slaves toil in labour pits beneath an obsidian ziggurat tower. The Chaos Dwarfs of the ash-choked Plain of Zharr worship Hashut. Their sorcerers know of wyrdstone, and some send raiders to Mordheim for slaves and loot.

LORE.name: Mountains of Mourn
LORE.status: Ogre mountains on the way to Cathay, with ancient giant ruins
LORE.text: A high mountain range of hostile weather and huge bears, home to tribes of Ogres and goblins living beside them. Ogres drift from here into foreign lands as hired muscle. Caravans fear the Ogres and the ruins of giant dwellings.

LORE.name: Nippon
LORE.status: Far eastern land of clans, samurai and ronin
LORE.text: A distant land south-east of Cathay, ruled by clans with samurai and ashigaru. Nipponese ronin sell their swords as caravan guards. Rare expeditions come to Mordheim for relics and knowledge as well as honour.

LORE.name: Ulthuan
LORE.status: Island kingdom of the High Elves
LORE.text: The elven isle in the far west, from where High Elf ships once explored the world, and whose traders now sail widely. It was once home to Nagarythe, from which the Dark Elves broke away. Its goods turn up in Marienburg's shops.

LORE.name: Nagarythe
LORE.status: Fallen High Elf kingdom, home of the Shadow Warriors
LORE.text: A once-rich High Elf kingdom that Malekith and Morathi led into Chaos worship. The loyal remnant fought a shadow war, then wandered as outcasts when Nagarythe was torn apart. Some of these Shadow Elves now seek fortune and revenge across the world.

LORE.name: Naggaroth
LORE.status: Harsh land of the Dark Elves
LORE.text: The cold, hard homeland of the Dark Elves (Druchii), who raid the world for slaves, gold and magic. Their ships hunt for wyrdstone and captives. They are feared more than Orcs.

LORE.name: Albion
LORE.status: Fog-bound isle of Ogham Stones, fens and storms
LORE.text: A misty island hidden from the world by thick fog, rich in rumoured treasure and the magic of its Ogham Stones. It has bogs, rain and storms, and dark and druidic wizards struggle there. Warbands usually find it by chance on a voyage.

LORE.name: Strigos
LORE.status: Lost realm of the Strigoi vampires and the Strigany
LORE.text: A once-rich kingdom under the 'undying king' Ushoran, ruined with Mourkain. Its descendants, the Strigany, wander in caravans through human lands and are often blamed for serving the vampire Strigoi. Strigoi now haunt graveyards with ghouls.

LORE.name: Brigandsburg
LORE.status: Rough encampment near Mordheim, full of Middenheimers and hired swords
LORE.text: One of the rival camps around the ruins, home to the shadier crowd, chiefly Middenheimers and Witch Hunters. It offers the most hired swords, at a discount, but the streets are dangerous. Marienburgers shun it as too filthy.

LORE.name: Norse Tribes
LORE.status: Seafaring Chaos-worshipping raiders of the far north
LORE.text: The Norse are the northern clans of Norsca: tall, fair and warlike people from a cold, mountainous coast haunted by mutant trolls and giants. They sail longships to raid the south and the far west, and many tribes serve the dark gods openly. With little loyalty beyond clan and ancestors they will also fight for pay. The clans that dwell farthest from the Realm of Chaos enjoy the least of their gods' favour, and that is why they are the ones most often met in the open in the lands of men.

LORE.name: Kurgan Tribes
LORE.status: Dark-skinned horse and hound tribes of the Northern Wastes
LORE.text: The Kurgan are a numerous, powerfully built people of the Northern Wastes, west of the Hung, and equally at home on foot or in the saddle. They come most eagerly and in the greatest numbers when Chaos hosts gather against the Old World, and the northernmost tribes are held to be the fiercest and most likely to win the gods' favour. Some tribes breed pit hounds to fight bears and trolls, and they craft bows from the bones of fallen foes. Having no ties to civilisation, they are never welcome on the farms and villages they raid.

LORE.name: Hung Tribes
LORE.status: Treacherous steppe horsemen who raid Cathay
LORE.text: The Hung are an eastern people, shorter and stockier than the Cathayans but alike to them in looks, and rated the finest riders anywhere. Their small, hardy horses thrive where bigger mounts would starve, so the tribes hunt mutant beasts in poor mountain country and gather strength for raids on the softer lands of Cathay to their south. Their loyalty to one another is famously thin, which keeps their warbands small.

LORE.name: Chaos Cultists of the Cathayan Borderlands
LORE.status: Mutated outcasts gathered around fallen wizards
LORE.text: Because the borderlands lie so close to the Realm of Chaos, many people there are touched by mutation. These outcasts gather around a fallen wizard seduced by dark rites and travel under cover, hiding their mutations as they slip into Cathay. They bring masques of plague and dances of contagion to each hamlet, using the empire as a place to practise their arts and sow future chaos.

LORE.name: Beastmen of the Northern Wastes
LORE.status: Hate-filled herds pushed out of the grasslands by Cathay
LORE.text: Tribes of beast mutants thrive between the Great Maw and the Warpstone Desert, on the edge of the bamboo groves of Cathay. Their bitter hatred of mankind, sharpened by the harsh land and by an empire that drove them from the grass, turns any small herd into a devastating raiding party. All they sometimes need is a leader with vision.

LORE.name: Beastmen Warbands of the Old World
LORE.status: Roaming herds that haunt the forests around Mordheim
LORE.text: Beastmen build no cities and obey no order, so they simply roam the great forests in small warbands led by the strongest of them, who is challenged and devoured when he weakens. Villagers around Mordheim say they outnumber men, and they raid isolated farms, tear down fences and walls, and soil crops for sport. A warband makes camp near roads, strikes once and moves on before any retaliation can reach it. Another account places Beastmen and Forest Goblins in the Forest of Shadows.

LORE.name: Carnival of Chaos
LORE.status: Plague-bringing travelling players who serve Nurgle
LORE.text: Rumour says this troupe began as a gypsy caravan, but it is now a wandering cavalcade of wagons whose players serve Nurgle. They give plays for rural villagers and at dusk throw off their disguises to reveal rotting daemons, spreading disease and carrying off survivors. The Carnival Master, a powerful sorcerer, calls up the daemons by sacrifice. Witch Hunters pursue it, but it always stays a step ahead.

LORE.name: The Dispossessed
LORE.status: Dwarf nobles who lost their hold and hunt treasure for a new one
LORE.text: When a hold falls to Goblins or Skaven, or a noble is banished for disgrace, the survivors are called the Dispossessed. Too proud to despair, such a noble gathers friends and kin to hunt treasure and hopes to win enough of a hoard to found a new hold. Dwarfs respect age, wealth and skill, and the greatest fortune in the Known World is said to lie in Mordheim, so that is where many of them go.

LORE.name: Dwarf Rangers of the Old Ways
LORE.status: Elder Dwarfs who distrust engineers and new-fangled arms
LORE.text: These Dwarfs believe the old ways are best and that gadgets from younger Dwarfs, especially the Engineering Guild, weaken the race. They are mostly older warriors, led by freshly made Runesmiths as keepers of tradition. Using only traditional weapons, they recover lost treasures and artefacts and cleanse fallen holds of the scum that has taken them. They are willing to ally with other Dwarf bands but never fully trust them.

LORE.name: Cult of Grimnir (Slayers)
LORE.status: Dwarfs who seek a glorious death against great monsters
LORE.text: Slayers join the cult of Grimnir for different reasons: to win back the honour of a failed clan, after being disowned, or to flee their past as in a foreign legion. The grimmest are those who have lost everything and have no kin to mourn them, and ironically they survive longest. They seek stronger foes and more desolate lands, younger Slayers follow them to learn, and the Giant Slayers teach in silence apart from their own Deathsong.

LORE.name: Black Dwarfs of Zharr-Naggrund
LORE.status: Hashut-worshipping Dwarfs who raid for slaves, metal and wyrdstone
LORE.text: The Dwarfs of Karak Vlag, cut off in holds under the ash plains of Zharr, turned in desperation to the bull-god Hashut and became sorcerer-smiths. They sell weapons and engines of metal and sorcery in exchange for food and captives, and drive slaves in the labour pits of Mingol Zharr-Naggrund. Their sorcerer-priests plan raids along the Silver Road for prisoners and hunt ore and wyrdstone, which is how some of their parties reach Mordheim.

LORE.name: Hashutsep's Expedition
LORE.status: A Chaos Dwarf sorcerer's quiet raid for slaves and witchstone
LORE.text: A sorcerer named Hashutsep in Zharr-Naggrund, hunting rivals to keep his powers, learned of Mordheim's fall. Seeing a city with no law and no defence against raids, he sent his best apprentices rather than a full invasion, to avoid his rivals' notice. Their aim is slaves, loot, and above all sorcerer's stone.

LORE.name: Kislevites
LORE.status: Brave northerners who hate Chaos and fight it without mercy
LORE.text: Kislev lies on the border of the Chaos Wastes, so every incursion passes through it first, and most Kislevites have lost homes or kin to Chaos. They are quiet with strangers but loud and merry among their own, and unforgiving toward any sign of Chaos worship. Close ties with the Empire send troops both ways.

LORE.name: Gryphon Legion
LORE.status: Kislevite noble knights garrisoned in the Empire
LORE.text: The Gryphon Legion is the pride of the Kislevite nobility, formed as a sign of the alliance between Kislev and the Empire. Its knights are all Kislevite nobles, but they are garrisoned and trained in the Empire.

LORE.name: Bergjaeger of Black Fire Pass
LORE.status: Mountain rangers and marksmen of the Averland pass guard
LORE.text: The Bergjaeger are a detachment of the Black Fire Pass guard, drawn from trappers and rangers of the surrounding mountains. They move silently over rock and serve as scouts. Many were gamekeepers, poachers pressed into service, or rustlers on the run, and all are expert marksmen. The pass is the only crossing between the Worlds Edge and Black Mountains and is infested with Night Goblins, trolls and Skaven.

LORE.name: Ostlander Freeswords
LORE.status: Poor, hardy, Taal-fearing villagers of an isolated province
LORE.text: Ostland is sparsely peopled and cut off from the rest of the Empire by the Forest of Shadows and the Middle Mountains, so its villages, mostly single extended families, live barely above subsistence. Married men farm and unmarried men trap, and Taal is widely worshipped. They love a brawl, hate Chaos fiercely after fighting beside Kislev in the Great War, and spend little coin on outsiders.

LORE.name: Orc Mobs
LORE.status: Brawling Greenskin bands drawn to Mordheim's loot
LORE.text: Orcs love fighting and looting above all, and spend their lives fighting each other or some other enemy. Mordheim offers an ambitious Orc Warboss both foes and plunder, so many mobs have been drawn to the wyrdstone. They would rather ambush rival warbands for their stones than dig for them. Few Hired Swords will serve them, knowing they might be eaten.

LORE.name: Black Orcs of the Waaagh!
LORE.status: Big, vicious Orcs scattered across the Empire after the Storm of Chaos
LORE.text: Black Orcs are bigger, smarter and better equipped than ordinary Orcs, and rumours about their origin say they were built rather than born. Many followed Grimgor Ironhide in his Waaagh! and now wander the Empire, where no one has the men to hunt them down. They have no plan but to fight whoever crosses their path.

LORE.name: Night Goblin Tribes
LORE.status: Cave-dwelling Goblins who infest the catacombs
LORE.text: Night Goblins prefer deep dark places and shun daylight, and tribes infest the Worlds Edge Mountains and the Black Fire Pass. In Mordheim they occupy the existing catacombs, grow fungus for food and poisons, and vandalise whatever they find. They bolster their numbers with cave squigs and, if lucky, a troll.

LORE.name: Forest Goblin Tribes
LORE.status: Stealthy poison users who live deep in the Great Forest
LORE.text: Forest Goblins have adapted to the Great Forest, using stealth and camouflage. They value gold only as a metal to coat their stone weapons, and a chieftain, usually the loudest Goblin, may send henchmen into an ambush just to collect their gilded weapons. Their poisons are said to surpass those of the Dark Elves, and they are rumoured to drive giant spiders into battle.

LORE.name: Amazons of the Heart of Darkness
LORE.status: Isolated jungle warriors who sacrifice every man they catch
LORE.text: The Amazons hold an island in a Lustrian river, covered in vines and overgrown pyramid ruins. They hunt Skinks for hides, hate men and the Norse above all, sacrifice captives to their gods and use salvaged Slann artefacts as weapons. Norse tradition holds that they descend from widows who left Skeggi and became Valkyries, and rumour credits them with an elixir of youth.

LORE.name: Amazon Fugitives
LORE.status: Enslaved warrior women who escaped the Old World's courts
LORE.text: Raiders such as Juan Cornetto's Tilean expedition carried Amazons off from Lustria and sold them in the courts and bazaars of the Old World. Count Steinhardt bought several hundred of them from slavers, and some got away from Mordheim during a feast and the city's destruction. They now live wild in the Empire, joined by runaways from travelling shows and from the fairs of Cutthroat's Den and the Black Pits. What they want is simply to get away.

LORE.name: Skeggi Colony
LORE.status: The first Norse settlement in Lustria
LORE.text: Skeggi was founded on Lustria's eastern coast by Losteriksson, the first expedition to reach the continent. Many of its warriors deserted in search of gold, leaving their wives behind. Skeggi's raiders still plague the coasts for riches and saga, and have pushed inland to plunder Slann temples.

LORE.name: Lizardmen Temple Guard
LORE.status: Skink and Saurus war parties defending the temple cities
LORE.text: Lizardmen and their Slann masters serve the departed Old Ones and keep to their rituals and plans. Temple Guardians, skink and saurus war-parties, fight guerrilla raids against plunderers on the beaches, jungle and ruined cities, helped by traps and mazes of tunnels. Huatl, Tlax and Xahutec are raided most often, and they are in constant conflict with Clan Pestilens.

LORE.name: Lustrian Reavers
LORE.status: Survivors of lost expeditions who claimed the jungle
LORE.text: Reavers are the toughest and most resourceful survivors of expeditions broken by disease, jungle beasts and Lizardmen. They keep the best gear salvaged from fallen comrades, scorn newcomers as rivals for the gold, and accept few recruits. When a Reaver dies, the survivors recover the arms and armour, choose a successor and induct him with a ceremony and plenty of Estalian wine.

LORE.name: Dark Elf Raiders
LORE.status: Druchii slavers who sail Black Arks for plunder and artefacts
LORE.text: The Druchii, evil kin of the High Elves, roam the Known World for slaves who are worked to death in mines, sacrificed to Khaine or tortured by the Brides of Khaine. In Lustria they come in Black Arks for Slann artefacts, striking from ambush before their victims know it. Rumour says they also reach Mordheim at night in black-sailed ships, craving wyrdstone and taking able-bodied prisoners as slaves.

LORE.name: Shadow Warriors of Nagarythe
LORE.status: Loyal exiles of the Witch King's former kingdom
LORE.text: Nagarythe's loyalists fought a secret war against Malekith and became wanderers, never welcome among other High Elves. Driven by revenge on the Witch King and his mother Morathi, they hunt Dark Elves and Chaos, and some serve as scouts for the Phoenix King. Some are sent on missions such as recovering relics left in the Old World, others are exiles or families on a vendetta.

LORE.name: Wood Elves of Athel Loren
LORE.status: Secretive forest guardians who rarely leave their realm
LORE.text: The Wood Elves left the other Elves long ago and live hidden in the enchanted forest of Athel Loren, in harmony with the seasons and as guardians of all things natural. They do not try to protect the world like High Elves or rule it like Dark Elves, but sometimes the will of their King and Queen, Orion and Ariel, sends them beyond the forest edge.

LORE.name: Miragleans
LORE.status: Tilean crossbowmen who hate Skaven
LORE.text: Miragliano's official weapon is the crossbow, and its warbands are deadly accurate with it. Three quarters of the city died in the red pox outbreak of 1812, and Miragleans have hated Skaven since.

LORE.name: Remasens
LORE.status: Tilean sailors who hate Dark Elves
LORE.text: In 1487 Dark Elf warships fell on the coastal city of Remas, and its people have hated the Druchii ever since. A Remasen warband will fight Dark Elves to the last man. Its officers are well trained and hard to shake.

LORE.name: Trantio Expeditions
LORE.status: The best-equipped human warbands in Lustria
LORE.text: The Lustria writer credits the famed explorer Stephanus Cornette and his brave Trantios with the setting. Warbands from Trantio are the best equipped and most experienced humans there, starting with extra gold.

LORE.name: Mazzalupo
LORE.status: Ragtag Tilean bands formed after the legendary wolf hunt
LORE.text: According to legend, a village in Tilea hired a wandering knight against a black wolf, and he gathered a fallen noble, a squire, a finance master, sheepherders and peasants who killed it. Since then such bands of vagabonds and rogues, held together by treasure or a feat that wins a lord's respect, are called Mazzalupo. Some end up in Mordheim from recklessness or because they are lost.

LORE.name: River Pirates of Mordheim
LORE.status: Pirate captains who raid ships and ruins through the fog
LORE.text: Pirate captains are drawn to Mordheim because the nearby rivers carry gold in and wyrdstone out. They use the permanent fog and dust to navigate the rivers through the city, appear from nowhere, loot a ship and vanish. Some have found safe harbours and send raiding parties into the ruins.

LORE.name: The Pit-Fighting Circuit
LORE.status: Illegal gladiator rings run by gambling cartels and guilds
LORE.text: Pit fights, outlawed in most regions, are kept alive by bribed officials and illegal gambling cartels, with merchant guilds earning on the side. They range from back-alley brawls to lavish contests near Mordheim, from Cutthroat's Haven to the Black Pits. Most fighters are slaves, trained hard, who hope to buy their freedom, and escapees form fugitive bands that make ideal hires for explorers of the ruins.

LORE.name: Nomad Tribes of Araby
LORE.status: Desert tribes with feuds and a fear of the Land of the Dead
LORE.text: Hundreds of tribes, from Tuareg to the legendary Muktarhin, roam the edge of the Araby desert, bound to oases. They have a strict honour code, and blood feuds can last generations. Stealing from a rival tribe is righteous, so they are feared raiders. Tales warn them from Nehekhara and Nagash, but a young sheikh seeking glory may lead his band into the Land of the Dead, from which many never return.

LORE.name: Tomb Guardians of Nehekhara
LORE.status: Undead retinues of the mummified kings of Khemri
LORE.text: Nehekhara was the first human civilisation, whose priests of the Mortuary Cult learned to mummify bodies so souls would last. Its kings were buried in huge pyramids in vast necropolises, with treasures from their lives. Nagash's ritual woke them as undead, and now Liche Priests and skeleton legions guard the tombs from all intruders.

LORE.name: Celestial Dragon Monks
LORE.status: Warrior monks guarding Cathay's borderland monasteries
LORE.text: In fortified monasteries on the slopes of Cathay's frontier, monks split their time between meditation, fishing, crafting and honing fighting techniques. Local peasants shelter near them against Ogres, Hobgoblins, Chaos marauders and beastmen. The army sees them as vigilantes but needs their skill, and they obey the emissary only because the Emperor commands it.

LORE.name: Merchant Caravans of the Silk Road
LORE.status: Risky overland trade convoys to Cathay and Ind
LORE.text: Merchants, guarded by sell-swords, gamble on the long trip east to Ind and Cathay through the Dark Lands and the Mountains of Mourn. Only one in ten succeeds, but a single venture can make a fortune, so many go again. The Silk Road was opened by the Tilean brothers Ricco and Robbio, and attracts Arabyan traders and Marienburg racketeers.

LORE.name: Maneaters
LORE.status: Ogre mercenaries who guard caravans and sometimes raid them
LORE.text: Ogres move in herds in tribes across the Mountains of Mourn, and wander abroad to hire out as muscle. Some raid merchants on the Ivory Road instead, and others agree to escort a merchant's caravan over long dangerous routes. A few such retinues reach Mordheim.

LORE.name: Nipponese Clan Expedition
LORE.status: Samurai warband led by a Hatamoto, far from home
LORE.text: A Hatamoto leads a clan warband of samurai and Ashigaru from Nippon to Mordheim, drawn by whispers of ancient relics and forbidden knowledge. They are bound by duty and honour and want to earn a place of honour in battle and honour their ancestors.

LORE.name: Questing Knights of Bretonnia
LORE.status: Knights who leave their domain to seek the Grail in Mordheim
LORE.text: To Bretonnian knights Mordheim is a vile place that needs virtue, so a quest there is a noble act. A Questing Knight gives up castle and domain, ranks above dukes, and is joined by Knights Errant and retainers. Dreams from the Lady of the Lake lead them, hoping for a drink from the Grail, and they fight the enemies of order.

LORE.name: Chapel Guard of the Lady
LORE.status: Defenders of the Lady's shrines and the damsels who tend them
LORE.text: Bretonnia is dotted with chapels, from cathedrals to woodsheds, that mark places sacred to the Lady of the Lake. Damsels and prophetesses tend them. If a chapel is threatened, a damsel sends for help, and knights, squires, peasant archers and pilgrims gather, or wandering warriors feel the call without a message.

LORE.name: Order of the Mare
LORE.status: Disgraced knights following the Prophetess of the Mare
LORE.text: A prophetess, called the Mare witch by some, claims descent from heroes of Gilles le Breton and restores honour to shunned knights, who swear loyalty to her as Paragons. She sends them to Mordheim for wyrdstone, joined by the Dames of the Mare, who have strange powers. Squires are raised early to knighthood and replaced by girls who join the Dames.

LORE.name: Imperial Gunnery School
LORE.status: Noble-born artillerists trained in Nuln
LORE.text: Nuln is known for handguns and war machines, and its Gunnery School trains gunners to use weapons invented by the Colleges of Engineering. Most students are younger noble sons with a talent for mathematics, who may stay to become Master Gunners. Every student does fieldwork, travelling anywhere under a Senior Gunnery Officer and an instructor, always well equipped.

LORE.name: Hochland Bandits
LORE.status: Refugee gangs hunting treasure in the Great Forest
LORE.text: After the Storm of Chaos, refugees from Hochland, Ostermark and Ostland crowded into Talabecland and clashed in Talagaad's streets. A bad winter and failing trade left men desperate, and rumours of treasure in the Great Forest sent gangs of petty crooks led by villains into the wilderness, where people have vanished.

LORE.name: Outlaws of Stirwood
LORE.status: Stirland fugitives who hide as archers in the forest
LORE.text: Stirwood lies north of Nuln and west of Wurtbad, where the Elector Count's law is enforced harshly, and even petty criminals are declared outlaws. Those who reach the forest band together, become fine archers by hunting the Count's deer, and ambush travellers. Sigmarite hermits tend them, and tales of Mordheim's riches reached them down the River Stir.

LORE.name: Horned Hunters of Taal
LORE.status: Forest worshippers who avoid cities and firearms
LORE.text: Horned Hunters prowl the woods in the Taalbaston crater and across Talabecland, loyal only to Taal. His rites demand great strength of body and mind, so they shun gunpowder and the works of science and see cities as errors. They dress like their god, in animal skins with antlers, and in Talabheim he is Father of Rivers.

LORE.name: Halflings of the Moot
LORE.status: Peaceful folk with a few restless adventurers
LORE.text: Halflings live in tight-knit communities and mostly want to eat, drink and be merry, but a village Elder sometimes grows restless and gathers like-minded folk to change the world. A few warbands march to Mordheim, dreaming of gold, wyrdstone and abandoned kitchens. One such tale is the Knights of the Kitchen Table, led by the rich archer Lord Charlie Gutbuckett.

LORE.name: Clan Eshin
LORE.status: Skaven assassins sent secretly into Mordheim
LORE.text: Skaven live in tunnels beneath human cities and have gathered warpstone for ages. The Nightmaster of Clan Eshin keeps Mordheim's secret from other clans and sends small silent warbands of poison users and assassins through secret tunnels instead of armies. Eshin methods resemble Cathayan monks and assassins, and the clan is said to nearly call Cathay home.

LORE.name: Clan Pestilens
LORE.status: Skaven who revel in plague and wield censers
LORE.text: Pestilens Skaven love filth and disease, and use their immunity to plagues against their foes. Plague priests, monks and novices stalk ruins swinging smoking censers, and the clan is locked in conflict with the Lizardmen of Lustria.

LORE.name: Clan Moulder
LORE.status: Skaven beastmasters who breed living weapons
LORE.text: Second in wealth only to Clan Skryre, Moulder makes living weapons from flesh, using warpstone to mutate and cross-breed monsters. Packmasters capture trolls, manticores and other beasts for the Master Moulders' experiments. They come from the Hell Pit in the north, to Mordheim for warpstone and to the Chaos wastes for new creatures.

LORE.name: Dreamwalkers of Morr
LORE.status: Dream-guided hunters of Undead and necromancers
LORE.text: Dreamwalkers are servants of Morr who believe their god sends dreams pointing out evils to crush. A band forms around a Priest of Morr or a Dreamer, whom a priest must certify, and Morr's temples support it. They are mostly human, middle-class Imperials, few but dedicated.

LORE.name: Priests of Morr in the Death's Head
LORE.status: Rivals called to Mordheim by visions of the death god
LORE.text: In the Procession of Morr, priests are summoned to Mordheim by troubled dreams, each sure the vision came from Morr himself. They distrust one another and recruit warbands before entering the city, for protection or hidden aims. The campaign is set in the Death's Head district, with its prison, chapels, graveyards and a large Temple of Morr.

LORE.name: Protectorate of Sigmar
LORE.status: Warrior-priests' personal guards sent to cleanse Mordheim
LORE.text: Every high-ranking Warrior Priest keeps an entourage of warriors as a personal guard, called the Protectorate. In peacetime they turn to problems inside the Empire, and Mordheim is such a place. The Grand Theogonist endorses the Witch Hunters but gives the Protectorate his full blessing and sends them into the city.

LORE.name: Sorcerous Societies
LORE.status: Secret wizard circles that survived the Wizard Wars
LORE.text: Magic users have long been suspect, and between 1982 and 1991 the cults of Sigmar and Ulric persecuted wizards in the Wizard Wars. Many fled or hid, and secret societies formed to protect magical teachings. They send members for artefacts and materials, to root out evil casters, and for other perilous tasks.

LORE.name: Masters of Horror
LORE.status: An exiled scientist and his created monsters
LORE.text: A scientist, once acclaimed, was cast out of Altdorf and now lives in a ruined tower in dead woods with a golem and mutated fiends. He wants to hurt those who expelled him, and needs wyrdstone to power his inventions, so he goes to Mordheim.

LORE.name: Court of the Profane Pleasures
LORE.status: Ostermark nobles corrupted by the Lord of Pleasure
LORE.text: When the Shadowlord demanded loyalty from Mordheim's hidden cultists, most kneeled willingly. Some Ostermark nobles had been corrupted by Slaanesh long before the comet. After the Cataclysm they emerged and hunt captives for rituals in the catacombs, drugging and lobotomising them. This draft comes from Tuomas Pirinen.

LORE.name: Blood Dragon Vampires
LORE.status: Honourable warrior vampires of Abhorash's line
LORE.text: The Blood Dragons are vampires said to descend from Abhorash, Lord of Blood. They are the most honourable bloodline and the closest to their human past: great warriors with a code of chivalry, rare in the Empire and found mostly in Bretonnia and the Blood Keep, which is said to lie in the Grey Mountains. They keep out of the politics of the other bloodlines.

LORE.name: Lahmian Sisterhood
LORE.status: Female vampires who rule by charm and infiltration
LORE.text: The Lahmians are almost all female, chosen for beauty, led by Neferata of the Cult of Blood in the Silver Pinnacle in the Worlds Edge Mountains. They compete with the von Carsteins but infiltrate high society with art and statesmanship rather than force, always trying to manipulate other families.

LORE.name: Necrarchs
LORE.status: Mad vampire necromancers who hoard dark lore
LORE.text: After Lahmia fell and the Great Library burned, a few Necrarchs fled with books and scrolls of Nagash's dark lore, and hid in towers to study. They are cadaverous loners who hate the living and dislike other vampires, and seek an end to all life. Mordheim's wyrdstone draws them from their towers.

LORE.name: Strigoi Ghoul Kings
LORE.status: Cursed bestial vampires ruling packs of ghouls
LORE.text: Strigoi vampires, the Cursed Ones, were cursed by other vampires and hate them. They are hunched brutes with ghoul courts in graveyards, who dream of destroying men and their kin. They descend from Ushoran, whose people the Strigany still remember.

LORE.name: Strigany
LORE.status: Wandering descendants of Strigos, blamed for serving vampires
LORE.text: After Mourkain's destruction the Strigany became nomads, who dream that Ushoran will return to reclaim their land. Superstitious people accuse them of serving Strigoi, and persecute and kill them, though some bands do have such a protector.

LORE.name: The Dark Brotherhood
LORE.status: Secret guardians of sleeping vampires in merchants' cellars
LORE.text: A brotherhood watches over vampires who sleep for centuries in coffins beneath the cellars of merchants and craftsmen, and waits for the hour to wake them. In Mordheim that hour has come, and the lords of the night walk the streets.

LORE.name: Grave Robbers
LORE.status: Tomb looters who flee the law into Sylvania
LORE.text: Grave robbers are harshly punished, so they flee to Sylvania where few lawmen follow. There the graves empty themselves and few return. Corpses sell well to dark arts and medical students, and experienced bands loot crypts of undead.

LORE.name: Vampire Hunters of Sylvania
LORE.status: Slayers and Morr priests who fight the von Carsteins
LORE.text: Under the von Carsteins, Sylvanians cower indoors at night and their dead rise from the cursed soil. Those few who escape may return with hunters trained against undead, and priests of Morr who want to cleanse the land's rulers. They leave ash behind.

LORE.name: Roadwardens
LORE.status: Marshals who patrol the Empire's roads from coaching inns
LORE.text: Roadwardens are tireless marshals who patrol the roads against bandits and highwaymen and report trouble. They use the stout coaching inns as bases, and those inns become centres of defence in times of unrest.

LORE.name: The Badlands
LORE.status: Barren waste between the Worlds Edge Mountains and the Black Gulf
LORE.text: A dry, rocky waste in the far south of the Old World, with weird rock spires and haunted ruins of the old Strigos empire. It holds more greenskin tribes than anywhere outside the Dark Lands, and ogres roam its south. Ghouls, carrion birds and Chaos hounds hunt on the plain. No traveller crosses it safely, whatever the escort. Dwarfs come here to look for a rumoured tunnel to the brightstone mines.

LORE.name: Troll Country
LORE.status: Bleak steppe and tundra in northern Kislev
LORE.text: The northernmost reach of Kislev, flat steppe that thins into tundra beneath the mountains at the edge of the Chaos Wastes. Nothing can be farmed and settlements are rare. Winter snow closes the paths, which also stops raiders. Nomad herders of several peoples live here, and beastmen and spirits roam too, but trolls rule the land: stone and river trolls in the south, mutated Chaos trolls farther north.

LORE.name: Nordland
LORE.status: Imperial province on the north-western coast
LORE.text: An electoral province of the Empire on its north-western shore, home of the Imperial Navy's Second Fleet. It joined the Empire late, after its Jutone people had refused Sigmar's offer. Tolled coast roads feed its government, and sea fortresses and watchtowers face the Norscan raiders who cross the Sea of Claws. Raid and counter-raid are part of its way of life. Salzenmund is its capital.

LORE.name: Wissenland
LORE.status: Southern province, the Empire's armoury
LORE.text: A founding electoral province in the south of the Empire, known as its armoury because it holds Nuln, the largest industrial city of the Old World, whose workshops turn out the realm's best black-powder weapons. After Solland was ruined in the Orc invasion of the early eighteenth century of the Imperial calendar, its lands passed to Wissenland, which still bears Solland's flag on its own banners in memory.

LORE.name: Ind
LORE.status: The Land of a Thousand Gods, a rich peninsula in the Far East
LORE.text: A great peninsula in the Far East, south of the Mountains of Mourn and south-west of Cathay. It is the nearest of the three human lands of the East to the Old World and draws spice merchants, though many never return. Wealthy lords live in grand palaces, the golden temples are many and the people honour a bewildering host of gods. Strange customs can anger locals, and bestial creatures and bloodthirsty cults wait along the way.

LORE.name: The Southlands
LORE.status: The Dark Continent far south of the Old World
LORE.text: A mostly tropical continent far south beyond Araby and the Land of the Dead. Its north is desert studded with empty tomb-cities, its south untouched jungle and swamp. Legend says it was once joined to Lustria before the Old Ones remade the continents. The hidden Lizardmen city of Zlatlan lies here, High Elves keep an outpost on its southern tip, and few explorers return from the interior.

LORE.name: The Ogre Kingdoms
LORE.status: The homeland of the ogres in the Mountains of Mourn
LORE.text: The scattered tribal realms on the slopes and valleys of the Mountains of Mourn, which every ogre calls home however far he wanders. Tyrants rule rival kingdoms there, warring and extorting tribute to feed the hunger of their god, the Great Maw. Ogre bands hire out as thugs and mercenaries across the world for gold and meat. They also broke the realm of the Skytitans and once held land on the Eastern Steppes.

LORE.name: Solland
LORE.status: Ruined province, now part of Wissenland
LORE.text: Once a southern province of the Empire, home of the Menogoth tribe whose sun emblem its nobles kept. An Orc Waaagh! under Gorbad Ironclaw wrecked it and killed its Elector Count in the early eighteenth century of the Imperial calendar. It later returned as the Barony of Sudenland, but was folded into Wissenland after the crisis of 2512. The River Sol was its border with Wissenland.

LORE.name: Estalia
LORE.status: Peninsula of rival kingdoms in the south-west Old World
LORE.text: A warm peninsula south of Bretonnia and south-west of the Empire, split among old rival kingdoms and proud cities, the chief ones being Bilbali in the north and Magritta in the south. Estalians are known for friendly merchants and skilful duellists. Their ruling families are bound by centuries of marriage, murder and betrayal. Orcs and beastmen come out of the Irrana Mountains, and undead land from the sea.

LORE.name: Sartosa
LORE.status: Anarchic pirate island south of Tilea
LORE.text: A walled island city off the Tilean coast near Luccini, run by pirates and a haven for outlaws, brigands and mercenaries. Press-gangs, duels and thieves fill the docks. A deadly current guards its northern shore, and only pirates know the way through the shifting Skull Sands to the south, a secret whose betrayal is punished horribly. Wrecked ships there count as free salvage under pirate law.

LORE.name: Luccini
LORE.status: Tilean city-state, boasting itself the oldest
LORE.text: A Tilean principality that claims to be the country's oldest city, built on an Elf-made acropolis by the twin rulers Lucan and Luccina, whom its people treat as divine. Luccini is a strong sea power with a large galley fleet, kept up against the pirates of nearby Sartosa. Its army is reckoned among the best in Tilea, and many mercenaries have trained here.

LORE.name: Pavona
LORE.status: Landlocked city-state in the middle of Tilea
LORE.text: A prosperous principality at the heart of Tilea on the plains between the River Remo and the Apuccini Mountains, with a mild climate but no coast. It rose to rival Trantio for the eastern trade with the Dwarfs, the Border Princes and the Silk Road, and the contested land between them became a hunting ground for mercenary captains. The ruling families made many short-lived marriage pacts.

LORE.name: Verezzo
LORE.status: Wealthy republic in the Tilean heartland
LORE.text: A rich republic in the centre of the Tilean peninsula, without a sea outlet and overshadowed by Remas and Luccini. Its story includes the Silk Road venture of 1699, when the merchant brothers Ricco and Robbio bought a Dragon-marked silk banner from Dwarfs in Karaz-a-Karak and wondered whether it showed an eastern way to Ulthuan. An earlier journey east by the explorer Marco Polare had been forgotten.

LORE.name: Karaz-a-Karak
LORE.status: Everpeak, capital hold of the Dwarf High King
LORE.text: The greatest and most populous of the Dwarf holds, hidden behind a winding pass in the Worlds Edge Mountains. The High King holds court in a hall vast enough to swallow a human town, and the city keeps the Great Book of Grudges, the Book of Remembering and enormous hoards of treasure. It has withstood countless attacks without ever falling. Even far-off Dwarfs speak of it with fierce pride.

LORE.name: Barak Varr
LORE.status: Gate to the Sea, the Dwarfs' harbour hold
LORE.text: The only Dwarf hold built as a port. From the clifftop it looks like ships will smash into the stone, but the tides of the Black Gulf have cut sea caves into the white rock where the Dwarf trading fleet is moored. The hold was founded at the mouth of the Blood and Skull rivers, and its fleet shows that a folk of miners can take to the sea, as outsiders find hard to believe.

LORE.name: Erengrad
LORE.status: Kislev's main trading port on the Sea of Claws
LORE.text: Kislev's biggest and busiest port at the mouth of the River Lynsk, second in the north only to Marienburg. It began as the walled Ungol town of Norvard, which the Gospodar armies overran. Ships from the Old World, the New World and even Norsca bring goods, slaves and gems. Kislev has no fleet, so Imperial warships and armed private vessels protect the waters, and the port is ringed with cannon, walls and sunken mines.

LORE.name: Praag
LORE.status: The Cursed City, bastion of northern Kislev
LORE.text: The largest and best fortified city in the north of Kislev, rebuilt again and again by stubborn, mostly Ungol townsfolk after each assault by Norscans and other Chaos forces. Constant contact with Chaos has brought mutation, madness and decay to the streets, yet the people refuse to leave. Rumour says something hidden in the city is why the powers of Chaos keep returning.

LORE.name: Carroburg
LORE.status: Glassmaking city on the Reik, in Middenland
LORE.text: A smaller Imperial city on the steep east bank of the River Reik, once seat of the Teutogen kings and capital of the old Drakwald province, later part of Middenland. It makes glass and pottery and lives from trade. The streets are a maze of stairs and winding lanes, and the richer a district, the higher up the hill it stands, which keeps the dockside boot cleaners busy.

LORE.name: Salzenmund
LORE.status: Capital of Nordland on the River Salz
LORE.text: The capital of Nordland, among hills where the tributaries of the River Salz meet, once a gathering place of the western Jutone people. Elector Counts built castles on the hilltops, among them the Jutone's Nest, whose keep needs no outer wall. It faces west to watch the Elves of Laurelorn. Its fairs and timber from the forest bring in trade, though business on the roads to Erengrad and Middenheim has lately dwindled.

LORE.name: Kemperbad
LORE.status: Free town on the east bank of the Reik, known for brandy
LORE.text: An old Imperial town in Reikland, famed for fine brandy. It is the only Reikland holding on the east bank of the Reik apart from Castle Reikguard. Reikland, Stirland and Talabecland nobles each ruled it by turns, until Emperor Boris Goldgather granted it a charter in 1066. A Council of Thirteen, with merchants and the temples of Sigmar and Shallya, has governed it as a free city since.

LORE.name: Laurelorn Forest
LORE.status: Magical forest of the Eonir on the northern Imperial coast
LORE.text: A magical forest on the northern coast of the Empire, west of Salzenmund and reaching to the border with the Wasteland. Middenland and Nordland both claim it, but its Eonir wood elves dare either to enforce the claim. They are an older, more open people than their kin in Athel Loren and keep traces of the first Ulthuani colonies. They are said to sympathise somewhat with the Dark Elves as outcasts.

LORE.name: The Sea of Claws
LORE.status: Cold, pirate-ridden sea between the northern Empire and Norsca
LORE.text: A bitterly cold and rough part of the Great Ocean that divides the northern Empire from Norsca, notorious for piracy. Ships still cross it in numbers from Marienburg and other northern ports, bound for Norsca or farther afield. The Dragon's Maw, a jagged line of rocky islets off northern Bretonnia, has broken many ships.

LORE.name: Zlatlan
LORE.status: The Hidden City of the Lizardmen in the Southlands
LORE.text: The greatest Lizardmen temple-city of the Southlands and one of the few still inhabited. Its Slann mage-priests lost their link to those of Lustria, because the telepathic line across the jungle pyramids cannot cross the ocean, so they work in isolation. Their calculations of the Old Ones' plans can drift out of step with Lustria's. The city is said to date from before the Old Ones split the continents.

LORE.name: Naggarond
LORE.status: The Tower of Cold, the Witch King's city
LORE.text: The oldest and largest city of the Dark Elves, ringed by black walls and a hundred towers at the foot of the Iron Mountains, and the seat of the Witch King Malekith. Heads and limbs rot on spikes outside as warnings. Inside lie mansions, barracks, slave pits and temples, where followers of Khaine cut out the hearts of living victims, so that murder seems to hang in the air.

LORE.name: Hag Graef
LORE.status: City of Shadows, second city of Naggaroth
LORE.text: A gloomy Dark Elf city at the bottom of a deep canyon, where sunlight never reaches the walls. Eight black towers rise from the canyon floor, linked by bridges and platforms of wood, bone, stone and spider silk, with whole districts on the larger platforms. Its mines hold veins of warpstone that animate the dead to labour. Hag Graef has grown so rich that it rivals Naggarond in power.

LORE.name: Har Ganeth
LORE.status: City of Executioners, fortress of the Khaine cult
LORE.text: A cursed Dark Elf fortress-city in the north of Naggaroth, devoted to Khaine, the elven god of murder. It was founded by exiles from Nagarythe after the Sundering and became the bloody centre of the Cult of Khaine, ruled by its Hag Queens. It is also known as the City of Executioners and the Fortress of Ice.

LORE.name: The Blighted Marshes
LORE.status: Rotten swamp in north-west Tilea, hiding the Skaven capital
LORE.text: A fen in the Tilean principality of Tobaro, running between the River Trino and the Abasko Mountains. Locals also call it the Zombie Marshes. The Skaven keep their buried capital, Skavenblight, far in its depths.

LORE.name: Skavenblight
LORE.status: The hidden Great City of the Skaven
LORE.text: The secret underground capital of the Skaven Under-Empire and birthplace of their race, half sunk in the rotten heart of the Blighted Marshes. It is the largest city in the world, a sprawl of caverns and tunnels on an unimaginable scale, kept hidden by powerful magic. The Lords of Decay rule from here, and the clans trade here, which draws every sort of thief and renegade.

LORE.name: Knights Panther
LORE.status: Famed knightly order of the Empire, born in the Araby crusades
LORE.text: A secular order of Imperial knights who hunt mutants and Chaos worshippers and defend the realm. It is among the three largest orders and the best known. It began in the Great Crusade against Araby, when knights pursuing the Sultan's remnants into the Atalan Mountains killed great wild cats and wore their pelts as cloaks. They brought living panthers home, and the Elector Counts recognised the order despite religious cults wanting only their own templars.

LORE.name: Reiksguard
LORE.status: Elite knights sworn to guard the Emperor
LORE.text: A secular order of heavy cavalry and infantry, first raised under Count Wilhelm III of Reikland to protect his line, now the core of the Emperor's household guard. Its knights swear to give their lives for the Emperor, whom they see as the living form of Sigmar. The Emperor may lend a unit to another Elector Count's army, as support or to keep an eye on an unsteady noble.

LORE.name: Knights of the Blazing Sun
LORE.status: Small elite order of Myrmidia's templars
LORE.text: A wealthy, small knightly order devoted to the war goddess Myrmidia, which prizes skill and record over noble birth and studies the craft of war. Its knights roam the Old World for battles. The order traces itself to the Great Crusade against Araby and rode early to join Magnus the Pious against Chaos. In recent centuries it has spread out from Tilea and Estalia.

LORE.name: Order of the Silver Hammer
LORE.status: Sigmarite witch hunters with the Grand Theogonist's commission
LORE.text: The state-sanctioned witch hunters of the Cult of Sigmar, feared by guilty and innocent alike. The Order of the Silver Hammer was formed by Grand Theogonist Siebold II, in a time of weak government, from warrior priests and investigators set on finding agents of Chaos. Each carried a letter under the Grand Theogonist's seal that opened any door.

LORE.name: Cult of Sigmar
LORE.status: The Empire's state church
LORE.text: The state church of the Empire, honouring its patron god Sigmar. It was founded in 73 of the Imperial calendar by the friar Johann Helstrum, who told of a vision of Sigmar crowned a god, and became its first Grand Theogonist. It grew into one of the most powerful forces in the realm, and Sigmar has partly replaced Ulric as the Empire's god of war.

LORE.name: Cult of Ulric
LORE.status: The cult of the god of war, winter and wolves
LORE.text: An ancient religion that is second only to the Cult of Sigmar, older than the Empire. Ulric is the fiercest of the Old World gods and is honoured mainly in the northern provinces and in Norsca. Its heart is Middenheim, where a great temple was built round a silver-white flame that never goes out. The cult holds white wolves sacred, and devotees wear long hair and rough beards like their god.

LORE.name: Cult of Myrmidia
LORE.status: Cult of the goddess of war and strategy
LORE.text: The religion of Myrmidia, goddess of war, strategy, honour and culture, favoured mostly by the southern lands. Her statues stand on nearly every street corner of Tilean and Estalian cities, and her name is called on against illness and beastmen alike. Soldiers pray to her before battle, and townsfolk and peasants for courage in the dark.
